# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | delete-block logic vs. worked example | 347-49 (0/3 ×3) | agent deletes only literally-blank rows above "Gross Pay"; gold deletes the whole section-separator block (blank rows + "Employee Info" label + header row). Instruction gives a concrete example ("delete rows 29 to 36") the agent never checks against. | BEHAVIORAL/KNOWLEDGE | STRUCTURE: mandatory "reproduce the instruction's worked example" verification item |
| 2 | wrong value TYPE written | 418-29 (float where int, 1 cell = only diff), 347-49 (str/int where float) | pandas upcasts int columns w/ blanks to float; dtype=object reads write numbers as strings | KNOWLEDGE/CONTRACT | prompt type-preservation rule + checklist type item |
| 3 | overwriting cells the task doesn't ask for | 52216 (flaky: 1 cell CHANGED that should stay original), 55457 (padded past end) | agent fills/changes cells inside range that gold leaves at original value/blank | CONTRACT | prompt "only change what's asked" rule + checklist item |
| 4 | declares "Done" without real verification | 55457, 347-49 (say "contains expected values" with no check) | soft step-3 wording ("confirm before finishing") is skippable | BEHAVIORAL | STRUCTURE: convert step 3 into an unavoidable pre-finish checklist |
| — | ENV/DATA DEFECTS (handed back, NOT fixed) | 55457, 32468, (374-9 cap) | see below | — | none |

## Changes made this iteration
| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1,4 | ordered procedure + checklist (STRUCTURE) | task_template.md | Rewrote the 3-step loop into an ordered procedure + a mandatory pre-finish checklist ("output file existing is NOT success"), incl. a "reproduce the instruction's concrete example, then generalize the pattern" item. Generalizes: any task whose instruction states an example (row numbers / before→after values) now gets logic-checked against it. | 160-6 (same delete class): its example is blank rows it already deletes → unchanged; all passing tasks already produce correct values so checklist passes first try |
| 2 | knowledge rule + checklist item (CONTRACT) | prompt.md + task_template.md | Preserve source cell TYPE: numbers as numbers (not "208.88"), int-valued numbers as int (pandas floats them via NaN), and keep text/date-like text/leading-zero labels as text (never coerce). | 47484 (writes "01" text) & 40467 (writes text label) explicitly protected by the "keep text as text" clause; 160-6 protected by the "don't coerce date-like text" clause |
| 3 | additive rule + checklist item (CONTRACT) | prompt.md + task_template.md | Only produce the cells the instruction asks for; leave other in-range cells at original value/blank; never pad with 0/defaults. | 53161/40467/47484 fill exactly their asked cells (unchanged); 160-6 writes explicit blanks (consistent) |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change → the trace it targets)
- 347-49 (all trials): agent's own verify shows "Employee Info"/"Gross Pay" header rows REMAIN above each match and it deleted only 1 blank row/group, yet instruction says "delete rows 29 to 36" (8-row block). New checklist item forces the code to reproduce rows 29–36 → must include the label+header rows → matches gold's whole-separator-block deletion; then generalize (no hardcoded 29–36, safe across variants 2/3).
- 418-29 (only diff = "1 cell float where int expected, HIGHER than expected"): answer range A1:B7 includes integer reference numbers; pandas read floats them (7355554.0). Type rule + checklist int-cast makes the agent write int → removes the sole mismatch on that variant.
- 347-49 (TYPE: 6 str-where-float, 6 int-where-float): dtype=object read wrote numbers as strings; type rule "write numbers as real numbers" corrects these cells.
- 52216 t0 ("1 cell CHANGED although expected is cell's own original input"): "only change what's asked / leave in-range cells untouched" rule + checklist item stops the spurious overwrite that only t0 committed (t1/t2 pass) → makes the good behavior consistent.
- Premature-Done (55457 msg6, 347-49 msg10 both assert success with no re-open check): step 3 is now a hard checklist gate ("output file existing is NOT success … reply without a code block ONLY after every item passes").

## Blast-radius per edit
- Checklist/procedure rewrite (task_template step 3): BOUNDED — it is a verification gate, not a behavior change; passing tasks already satisfy every item so their trajectory is unchanged. Named passing tasks checked: 47484, 40467, 53161, 160-6.
- Type-preservation rule: BOUNDED/ADDITIVE — only constrains the type of values already being written; the "keep text as text / don't coerce" half is exactly what protects 47484, 40467, 160-6 (the 2026-08-18 regression that broke 160-6 was a "convert to real dates" rule — this rule does the OPPOSITE, forbidding coercion).
- "Only change what's asked" rule: BOUNDED/ADDITIVE — narrows to unrequested/padding cells; passing tasks write only their asked cells.

## Process & features used
- Serial (single agent): the failing set is 6 tasks and required cross-referencing prior verified ground-truth knowledge; read all 9 tasks' traces + 4 passing tasks directly rather than fanning out.
- Prior knowledge used (persistent memory, verified in earlier runs): 55457 = EMPTY instruction (unwinnable); 32468 = corrupted gold (unwinnable); 374-9 capped ~1/3 by a double-count gold defect; 347-49 fixable = delete whole separator block anchored on "Gross Pay"; REFUTED lever = "write Excel formula instead of literal" regressed 52216/53161 (did NOT re-try); REFUTED lever = "write real dates not strings" broke 160-6 (did NOT re-try — my type rule forbids that coercion).

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- "Prefer LITERAL values over formulas" (memory: formula lever regressed cell-level lookups; all-or-nothing on recalc).
- The "keep text as text / never coerce date-like text or leading-zero labels" clause — it is the guard that keeps 160-6, 47484, 40467 passing.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- 55457 — DATA DEFECT: instruction field is empty; no prompt can supply the missing task. Reward 0 is a benchmark defect, not a capability failure.
- 32468 — DATA DEFECT: gold is corrupted (SUMIFS computed on a mutated source cell); cell-level all-or-nothing ⇒ unwinnable by any method.
- 374-9 — capped ~1/3 by a double-count gold defect on 2/3 variants; agent already reads cached values via pandas, so the recoverable read bug is not present here. Left to the general checklist (may steady variant-1 pass) but no dedicated edit.
